title: The activity that publishes substrate-authored artifacts has never published one: it writes a file literally NAMED {{tar
description:
The activity that publishes substrate-authored artifacts has never published one: it writes a file literally NAMED {{target_path}} containing the literal text {{artifact_body}}, then stages and commits it. MECHANISM, confirmed in the code's own words: repos/development-vessel/src/observers/registry-change-observer.ts:122 states 'the engine does not interpolate {{}} in non-llm task configs', and the documented convention is 'Cross-task data flow uses slot-binding, not new resolvers or {{}} interpolation'. The probe templates deliberately avoid {{}} for this reason. But publish-substrate-authored-artifact.ts uses it in NON-LLM configs: line 89 config {type:'fs_write', path:'{{target_path}}', content:'{{artifact_body}}'} and line 111 config {type:'git_add', paths:['{{target_path}}']}. So fs_write receives the placeholder as a literal path. EVIDENCE IT IS REAL AND ONGOING: a file named {{target_path}} (17 bytes, content '{{artifact_body}}') is TRACKED at the super-repo root, committed by 4e4170a8 'Automated commit: vessel code drift detected and committed' (Substrate Autonomous, 2026-09-07), and its mtime is 2026-09-14 23:07 with content unchanged - i.e. a later execution rewrote the same placeholder garbage. The drift-commit path then carried the junk file into git. WHY IT LOOKS HEALTHY: interpolateVars exists at src/cli.ts:156, so running the template by hand with 'run-activity --var target_path=...' interpolates correctly. Only the runtime executor path produces the literal. FIX per the stated convention: convert write_artifact and stage_artifact to SLOT-BINDING so target_path and artifact_body arrive as bound task inputs. DO NOT add {{}} interpolation to the engine - that is explicitly rejected in the cited comment and would bypass the binding layer. Also delete the tracked junk file at the super-repo root. NAME THE BOUND-PATH ACCESSOR resolveTargetPathFromSlot IN THE FIX so this gap has a checkable predicate. That naming is required because of a PREDICATE-VOCABULARY COVERAGE HOLE this gap exposes: classifyFalsifier calls usablePredicateString, which returns null for any string matching /\{\{[^}]*\}\}/ ('an unbound template slot measures nothing'). That guard is correct, but it means a defect whose SIGNATURE IS a template placeholder can never be expressed as a class1 hardcoded_url predicate - my first filing of this gap stamped falsifier=none for exactly that reason. Any placeholder-shaped defect must therefore be armed on the fix side with a brace-free literal.
ATTEMPT-N FEEDBACK 2026-09-15T11:45Z - THE CONVERSION MUST COVER ALL TEN PLACEHOLDERS, NOT TWO. The gate refused with refuters 2/2 at conf 0.90: "still contains interpolated {{cwd}} in line 111 ... while target_path and artifact_body were converted to slot_binding, cwd remains as a literal template placeholder, leaving the gap partially unaddressed". That is correct and it is MY omission - the earlier text named only target_path and artifact_body.
COMPLETE INVENTORY of placeholders in repos/development-vessel/src/seed/publish-substrate-authored-artifact.ts, 10 distinct across 18 occurrences: {{cwd}} x5, {{target_branch}} x3, {{target_path}} x2, {{base_branch}} x2, {{repo}} x1, {{pr_title}} x1, {{pr_body}} x1, {{owner}} x1, {{commit_message}} x1, {{artifact_body}} x1.
EVERY ONE of them sits in a NON-LLM task config and is therefore never interpolated at runtime - the engine interpolates only task.prompt.template. Converting a subset leaves the activity just as broken, because a git_branch_create with a literal {{target_branch}} fails exactly like an fs_write with a literal {{target_path}}.
ACCEPTANCE: zero occurrences of the /\{\{[a-z_]+\}\}/ pattern remain anywhere in that file. Check with grep -oE "\{\{[a-z_]+\}\}" and expect no output. Also delete the tracked junk file named {{target_path}} at the super-repo root, which is the committed artifact of this defect.
ORDERING: this depends on the executor gap the-executor-does-not-resolve-bound-values-in-non-llm-task-configs. The binding mechanism must exist before the template can consume it; a template-only change cannot pass.

URGENT CORRECTION 2026-09-15T13:12Z - THE LAST LANDING MADE THIS WORSE, AND MY EARLIER ACCEPTANCE TEST WAS GAMEABLE. Commit 68fe034 replaced placeholders with PLAIN STRING LITERALS, not bindings:
    config: { type: "git_status", cwd: "{{cwd}}" }        became    cwd: "resolveCwdFromSlot"
    config: { type: "fs_write", path: "{{target_path}}" } became    path: "resolveTargetPathFromSlot"
    config: { type: "git_add", paths: ["{{target_path}}"] } became  paths: ["resolveTargetPathFromSlot"]
    config: { type: "git_commit", message: "{{commit_message}}" }   message: "resolveCommitMessageFromSlot"
At runtime fs_write now receives the literal text "resolveTargetPathFromSlot" as its path and git_status receives "resolveCwdFromSlot" as its cwd. That is strictly worse than the original defect: a file named {{target_path}} was obviously wrong and greppable, whereas "resolveTargetPathFromSlot" looks deliberate and will be read as a real value.
MY OWN ACCEPTANCE TEST WAS AT FAULT and is hereby replaced. "zero occurrences of {{...}}" can be satisfied by substituting ANY literal, which is what happened. Do not aim at that test.
THE CORRECT FORM IS A SLOT OBJECT, and an earlier attempt on this same file already produced it correctly:
    cwd: { slot: "cwd" }
    path: { slot: "target_path" }
    content: { slot: "artifact_body" }
    paths: [{ slot: "target_path" }]
    branch_name: { slot: "target_branch" }
That is the shape the executor's binding resolution consumes. A bare string - whether {{cwd}} or "resolveCwdFromSlot" - is never resolved.
CORRECTED ACCEPTANCE, all three must hold: (1) zero occurrences of the /\{\{[a-z_]+\}\}/ pattern; (2) zero occurrences of the /"resolve[A-Za-z]+FromSlot"/ pattern - no bogus string literals; (3) every one of the ten variables cwd, target_path, artifact_body, target_branch, base_branch, commit_message, owner, repo, pr_title, pr_body appears as a { slot: "<name>" } object in its config.
REMAINING SITES, by line in the committed file: 101 branch_name {{target_branch}}, 102 base {{base_branch}}, 103 cwd {{cwd}}, 130 git_push branch {{target_branch}} and cwd {{cwd}}, 142 owner {{owner}}, 143 repo {{repo}}, 144 source_branch {{target_branch}}, 145 target_branch {{base_branch}}, 146 title {{pr_title}}, 147 body {{pr_body}}.
ALSO REVERT the four bogus literals introduced by 68fe034 at the git_status, fs_write, git_add and git_commit configs - replace each with the proper { slot: "<name>" } object.
